data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only under an installation ritual that requires the test to fail before the subject exists, and the 3-of-26 result is the number of tests that were never shown to fail; compile.py's 1/9 is the only module where the shown-to-fail-first installation was actually performed, while the 4/4 to 6/7 modules were tested after the fact, so their guards described the code rather than constraining it.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the test is written before the code but the code is written to make the test pass, the test still constrains.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the test is written after the code but the author genuinely does not know what the code does, the test can still constrain.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4 to 6/7 modules had their tests written first, the installation-order explanation fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the registry does not record test creation time, this claim is untestable from the available evidence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The installation ritual is the key variable, not the test's content. When a test is written before the code, its failure is the specification. When it is written after, its failure is a bug report. The 3-of-26 survivors are the tests written after the code they guard, so they were never shown to fail and therefore never constrained anything. The 1/9 lost mutation in compile.py is the one case where the shown-to-fail-first installation was performed but the mutation was in the installation ritual itself, not in the subject.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
